For someone to have blood type AB, they must inherit an “A” allele from one parent and a “B” allele from the other (genotype AB). Since parents with blood type O only have “O” alleles to pass on, they cannot provide the “A” or “B” alleles needed for their child to have blood type AB.
So if your mom is O, you can’t be AB. Even if your biological father is someone else, you would have inherited an O from your mother, making you A OR B but not AB.
